artifact.self_contained_problem:
For each positive integer $n$, define
$$a_n \;:=\; \frac{1}{n(2n+1)}\binom{2n}{n}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(51k+7)\binom{2k}{k}^{2}\binom{3k}{k}\,(-123)^{n-1-k}.$$
Prove or disprove the following statements.

(i) For every integer $n>1$, the integer $(-1)^{n-1}a_n$ is a positive integer, except when $2n+1$ is a power of $3$, in which case $3a_n$ is an integer not divisible by $3$.

(ii) For every prime $p>3$ and every positive integer $a$,
$$p^{a}\sum_{k=0}^{p^{a}-1}\frac{51k+7}{(-123)^{k}}\binom{2k}{k}^{2}\binom{3k}{k}\;\equiv\;7\bigl(p^{a}+p^{a-1}\bigr)-\tfrac{5}{6}\,p^{2}B_{p-2}(1/3)\pmod{p^{3}},$$
where $B_{m}(x)$ denotes the $m$-th Bernoulli polynomial.

(iii) For every prime $p>3$,
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{2k}{k}^{2}\binom{3k}{k}}{(-123)^{k}}\;\equiv\;
\begin{cases}
x^{2}-2p\pmod{p^{2}} & \text{if }\bigl(\tfrac{p}{3}\bigr)=\bigl(\tfrac{p}{17}\bigr)=1\text{ and }4p=x^{2}+51y^{2}\text{ with }x,y\in\mathbb{Z},\\[2pt]
2p-3x^{2}\pmod{p^{2}} & \text{if }\bigl(\tfrac{p}{3}\bigr)=\bigl(\tfrac{p}{17}\bigr)=-1\text{ and }4p=3x^{2}+17y^{2}\text{ with }x,y\in\mathbb{Z},\\[2pt]
0\pmod{p^{2}} & \text{if }\bigl(\tfrac{p}{3}\bigr)=-\bigl(\tfrac{p}{17}\bigr),
\end{cases}$$
where $\bigl(\tfrac{\cdot}{\cdot}\bigr)$ is the Legendre symbol.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search located the original list of conjectures by Z.-W. Sun (which contains this conjecture A20) and several follow-up papers proving "three conjectures on congruences" of Sun, but no specific source confirming a proof of all three parts of this particular conjecture (the integrality of $a_n$, the mod $p^3$ supercongruence, and the mod $p^2$ evaluation involving $4p=x^2+51y^2$ and $4p=3x^2+17y^2$) was found. Status is therefore inconclusive.
